rows.name: launch-cancelled-restored

rows.name: recovery-writing
rows.how: a Steam switch killed while it was writing. No knob parks a switch between its snapshot and the start of the launcher (a few milliseconds), so the confirm click is sent without waiting for its answer, switch.json is watched, and killHard follows the first entry that names the snapshot; the journal the app left names a write step (file). A kill that lands after the journal has moved on to the start step is undone with Restore snapshot in the prompt and the switch is run again, three times at most

rows.name: recovery-signing-in
rows.how: the fake Epic launcher never signs in (the reactMs knob), so the switch waits in its sign-in phase; the app is killed there and started again

rows.name: recovery-rollback-failed
rows.how: an Epic switch that fails after its write (the processes.startFails knob: the fake launcher never comes up) and whose rollback fails too: while the switch waited for the launcher, the Config folder of its snapshot was moved aside in the scratch data folder, so the restore found no file; once the app had written rollbackFailed to switch.json the folder was moved back, the app closed and started again. Nothing in switch.json was written by the capture

rows.name: recovery-no-snapshot

rows.name: recovery-restored

rows.name: recovery-restore-error
rows.how: the switch parked and killed as for row 103, and the app restarted with the fake Epic launcher running (the processes.running knob); the answer to recovery:restore held in main until the dialog had painted "Restoring…" and its disabled buttons had dropped the focus, then released. The refusal is the adapter's own
